claims.object_text: inhibitor of TGF-β signaling pathway; nucleocytoplasmic transcription factor essential for forebrain development
claims.quote: Forkhead box G1 (FOXG1, also known as BF1), a member of the FOX family and an inhibitor of TGF-β signaling pathway, is a nucleocytoplasmic transcription factor that is essential for forebrain development.

claims.object_text: localized in oocytes, theca cells and corpora lutea
claims.quote: FOXG1 is localized in oocytes, theca cells (TCs) and CLs.

claims.object_text: expressed at all stages during early embryogenesis from zygote to blastocyst
claims.quote: After fertilization, FOXG1 is expressed at all stages during early embryogenesis, from zygotes to blastocysts.

claims.object_text: expression significantly increased following gonadotropin administration in immature mice
claims.quote: Following gonadotropin administration in immature mice, the expression of Foxg1 significantly increased along with steroidogenic genes, including Star, Hsd3β, Cyp11a1, as well as Cyp17a1 and Cyp19a1.

claims.object_text: silencing reduces testosterone and estrogen concentrations in cultured primary granulosa cells and theca cells
claims.quote: silencing of Foxg1 significantly reduced the concentration of testosterone and estrogen in cultured primary granulosa cells (GCs) and TCs (P < 0.05).

claims.object_text: silencing reduces expression of estrogen synthesis genes including Cyp17a1 and Cyp19a1
claims.quote: the expression level of genes that are critical in estrogen synthesis were significantly reduced after Foxg1 silencing, including Cyp17a1 and Cyp19a1.
